_comment: Cross-driver logger PARITY corpus of the 2026-11-20 logger-engines campaign (docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-20-logger-engines/report.md). Each section pins one rule the drivers had drifted on; every driver suite named in a section's `drivers` replays it, and a section a driver cannot replay names why in `not_replayed`. behaviour_vectors.json beside it pins filtering, the ring and both suppression layers; test_vectors.json pins the line format.

level_setting._comment: LOG-01. The stored script.log_level value selects the threshold of its declared name, matched without case; anything else selects the manifest default and is refused visibly. `default` must equal the manifest's (test-logger-scalars-single-source.cjs). Replayed through LoggerResolveLevel (Windows) and _shared/core/logger/engine/level_setting.lua (macOS Logger.apply_level_setting, Linux script_settings).

detailed_log._comment: The Debug menu's « Detailed log » switch (maintainer, 2026-11-24) replaces the log-level selector over the same script.log_level value: it reads ticked when the stored value's threshold lets through more than the default's, and a click stores the default when ticked, else DEBUG. Replayed through LoggerIsDetailed / LoggerDetailedToggleTarget (Windows) and _shared/core/logger/engine/level_setting.lua is_detailed / detailed_toggle_target (macOS, Linux).

format_failure._comment: LOG-02. A format error keeps the line and records the failure on it: the template, then the marker, the error text, and how many arguments were lost. The shared Lua core (macOS, Linux) used to write the bare template, indistinguishable from a normal line. Each language has its own template syntax; the object argument is what makes both formatters raise (an AHK Map, a Lua table under %d).

dated_retention._comment: LOG-03. A dated archive (ErgoptiPlus_<date>.log, ErgoptiPlus_errors_<date>.log) is purged when its date is older than today minus retention_days, compared as calendar days, whatever the time of day. macOS (the native worker and the Lua boot purge) compared the file's noon with now minus N x 86400 s, so the N-days-old archive vanished after noon only.

topical_retention._comment: LOG-04. A topical file (no date in its name) is a view of today: one last modified on another calendar day is removed by the retention pass. Linux kept it until it was N + 1 days old, so a topic that logged nothing today still showed an older day's lines. macOS retired its topical sub-files (one daily log only, 2026-11-25): its purge deletes the retired names whatever their age.

sink_failure._comment: LOG-05. A sink that raises loses the line it raised on, but not silently: the next line it accepts is followed by one WARNING from [logger] counting the lost lines and quoting the last error. The shared Lua core used to discard the error with nothing written anywhere.

not_replayed.windows: The Windows sink is the pending queue: a refused append keeps its lines and retries them, and the queue cap reports the lines it dropped (LOGGER_PENDING_CAP, test_logger.ahk).

sink_failure.report_template: %d %s refused by the log sink before this one (last refusal: %s).
